sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Zone
FROM ops.zones z
WHERE z.LocationID NOT IN (SELECT t.RatecodeID FROM lake.trips t WHERE t.PULocationID = z.LocationID)
ORDER BY z.LocationID

hypotheses.claim: NOT IN over a subquery forces a null-aware anti join, which is expensive. (matched: not in (select t.ratecodeid from lake.trips t where t.pulocationid = z.locationid) order b)

The LEFT_DELIM_JOIN (left anti join) is costly because it must handle potential NULLs in RatecodeID (NOT IN semantics), forcing a delimiter join that materializes the subquery results and prevents join elimination or predicate pushdown.

The inner HASH_JOIN between trips and DELIM_SCAN processes the full trips table (495k rows) and builds a hash table on PULocationID, which dominates CPU and memory usage; an index on trips.PULocationID could replace this with an index lookup.

The FILTER node after the left anti join evaluates a NULL-aware condition for each row, adding per-row overhead that could be avoided if the subquery were rewritten as a NOT EXISTS with a correlated join.
